promoted: {rival} is promoted to {title}. The congratulatory email reaches you too, as a courtesy.
{rival} is now {title}. Your intake's group chat hears about it before you do.
{rival} makes {title}. {They} sent round a very nice message, which you have read twice.
winService: There was one promotion slot at your grade this year. It went to you. {rival} sent congratulations within the minute, which is how you know the news reached {them} first.
The ranking exercise had room for one of you at this grade. It was you. {rival} took it well, in the sense that nobody saw {them} take it.
loseService: There was one promotion slot at your grade this year. It went to {rival}. You are told it was "very close", which is what they tell everyone, including {rival}.
The ranking exercise had room for one of you at this grade. It was {rival}. Your reporting officer says you are "next in line", and does not say for what.
winPolitics: There was one appointment at your level this year. It went to you. {rival} was the first to shake your hand at the swearing-in, and held it a beat longer than necessary.
losePolitics: There was one appointment at your level this year. It went to {rival}. The Prime Minister's Office describes the decision as "finely balanced".
pm: {rival} is to be the next Prime Minister. {They} telephoned you before the announcement, or said {they} did.
pmBlocked: The office above yours is occupied. {rival} is Prime Minister, and shows no sign of having considered the private sector.
The office above yours remains occupied. {rival} has announced a ten-year plan, which you are choosing to read as a policy document.
elected: {rival} was introduced at a press conference as a new candidate, and won. Your batchmate is now a Member of Parliament.
lostSeat: {rival} stood for Parliament and lost the ward. A month later {rival} was back in the service at the same grade, which everyone agreed to call a homecoming.
consultancy: {rival} is leaving for the private sector. The farewell lunch is at a hotel, which is how you know the package is good.
scandal: {rival} has resigned, for personal reasons. Everyone has a theory. Nobody says it in the lift.
rankedBelowService: The ranking exercise put {rival} above you this year. Neither of you went up. The slot went to someone from another division whom you have never met.
You were ranked just below {rival} this year, which is the one comparison nobody needed to make out loud. Nobody made it out loud.
rankedBelowPolitics: When the appointments were settled, {rival}'s name was ahead of yours on the list. Neither of you moved. Someone from the back bench did.
appointed: {rival} is appointed {title}. The swearing-in photograph is on the front page, and you are in the background of it.
{rival} is now {title}. Your intake's group chat hears about it before you do.
promotedApart: {rival} is now {title}. You hear about it at a dinner, from someone who assumes you already knew.
{rival} is now {title}. Your intake's group chat hears about it before you do.
electedTogether: {rival} stood at the same general election, in another constituency, and won. Your batchmate is now a Member of Parliament too.
lostSeatTogether: {rival} stood at the same general election, in another constituency, and lost. A month later {rival} was back in the service at the same grade, which everyone agreed to call a homecoming.
consultancyPolitics: {rival} has resigned {their} seat for a board appointment. The by-election is described as a referendum on nothing in particular.
scandalPolitics: {rival} has resigned from Parliament, for personal reasons. Everyone has a theory. Nobody says it in the lobby.
retired: {rival} retires as {title}. There is a farewell lunch. You send a card, and mean it.

folder.item: a peer assessment of {rival} that did you more good than it did {them}

events.title: The 360
events.body: It is 360-degree feedback season. You have been asked to assess {rival}, who joined in your intake and turns up at every meeting that matters. The form promises anonymity. It has a free-text box headed "Areas for development".

choices.outcome: Three sentences on stakeholder management, true and mildly painful. {rival} acts on all three within a year and never learns where they came from.
It is accurate. It is also the only peer comment the ranking panel quotes. {rival} is described that year as "still developing", which you did not write but did cause.
The form accepts it. HR's report later notes "limited peer input" for your whole division, which is the one comment that applies to you.

events.title: Annex B
events.body: {rival}'s paper for the Permanent Secretary goes up at nine tomorrow. You are copied for information. Annex B has the right numbers in the wrong columns, and the recommendation rests on them.

choices.outcome: {rival} fixes it at 11:50pm and says thank you twice, the second time in a voice you have not heard before.

choices.text: Say nothing. It is not your paper.
choices.outcome: The Permanent Secretary finds Annex B in four minutes. For the rest of the year {rival} is described as "detail-light". You are described as nothing at all, which this year is better.

choices.text: Raise it at the meeting, helpfully.
choices.outcome: You are thanked for your rigour. {rival} thanks you too, later, in the corridor, in a tone the minutes would not have captured.

events.title: One Posting
events.body: There is one two-year posting to the Budget Division at Finance this cycle, and your division has two nominees: you and {rival}. HR suggests the two of you "have a conversation" first, which in HR means one of you should withdraw.

choices.text: Withdraw, and say it was your idea.
choices.outcome: {rival} goes to Finance. Three weeks later a photograph arrives of the view from {their} new office, which is, admittedly, a very good view.

choices.text: Let HR decide on the files.

contest.winText: The posting goes to you. {rival} says {they} had expected it to, which may even be true.
contest.loseText: The posting goes to {rival}. HR's email to you uses the phrase "many strong candidates". There were two.

choices.outcome: HR decides on the files, which takes six weeks and a matrix.

choices.text: Make your case to the Director, privately.

contest.winText: The posting goes to you. {rival} hears, eventually, how.
contest.loseText: The posting goes to {rival}. The Director mentions, in passing, that {rival} did not come to see her about it.

choices.outcome: The Director listens, nods, and says she will "bear it in mind", which is the most anyone has ever got from her.

events.title: Views Are Sought
events.body: {rival} has been shortlisted for a post one grade above you both. The panel has asked for views from {their} peers. Yours will be read, and filed, and remembered by someone.

choices.outcome: You write half a page and mean all of it. Someone on the panel later shows it to {rival}, who never mentions it to you and never forgets it.
Two lines, both true, neither memorable. The panel files them with the others.

choices.text: Suggest, carefully, that another year at grade might help {them}.
choices.outcome: The panel finds your view "balanced". {rival} learns of it eventually, the way everyone here learns everything: from someone who was not supposed to say.

events.title: Saturday
events.body: {rival}'s ward has had a difficult year: a lift upgrading that overran, and a Forum letter a week. {They} asked whether you would walk the ward with {them} on Saturday morning. Your own ward has a walkabout planned for the same morning.

choices.outcome: Six blocks, two markets, and one auntie who assumes you are {rival}'s campaign manager and tells you exactly what she thinks of {them}. The letters to the Forum stop by March.
Your volunteers are better at it than you are. {rival} thanks them by name, which you notice.
Your ward is pleased to see you. {rival} manages without you, and remembers the Saturday.

events.title: First Among Equals
events.body: The question of the next generation's first among equals is being settled, informally, by people in a room. It has come down, as your intake joked at its first dinner, to the two of you.

choices.outcome: You say it plainly, to the people who need to hear it. {rival} says it too, in the next room. It will be decided the way these things are: slowly, and then all at once.
{rival} thanks you once, in private, and never again, which is how you know it was understood.

events.title: The Name Put Forward
events.body: {rival}, senior to you now, has been asked for names for a cross-ministry task force that everyone understands to be a proving ground. {They} put yours first.

choices.outcome: Lunch, on you, at a place {rival} chose. It was more expensive than {they} let on, and worth it.

choices.text: Decline. You would rather go up on your own file.
choices.outcome: {rival} says that is fair. It is, and it costs you a year.
